proposed_widenings.name: item_form_state_machine
proposed_widenings.justification: The item exists in three discrete forms (quarterstaff, 6-inch rod, 10-foot pole). Properties 'Acrobatic Assist', 'Attack Deflection', and 'Ranged Weapon' are form-conditional. No existing mechanics family can express form-conditional grant activation — EquipmentPredicate only covers wearing_armor / wielding_weapon, not 'current form of this item'. This requires a form-state subgraph: a set of named modes with associated grant lists, switchable by a bonus-action activation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: In certain forms, the weapon has the following additional properties. Acrobatic Assist (Quarterstaff and 10-Foot Pole Forms Only). Attack Deflection (Quarterstaff Form Only). Ranged Weapon (Quarterstaff Form Only).

proposed_widenings.name: RollKind.damage_roll
proposed_widenings.justification: The +2 weapon bonus applies to both attack rolls and damage rolls. RollKind covers attack_roll, saving_throw, ability_check, initiative, death_saving_throw — but not damage_roll. The damage bonus cannot be encoded without this variant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You have a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_thrown_property
proposed_widenings.justification: The quarterstaff form gains the Thrown weapon property with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 120 feet. No existing atom grants a weapon property. This is mechanically distinct from grant_speed, modify_speed, or force_move.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This weapon has the Thrown property with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 120 feet.

proposed_widenings.name: return_to_hand
proposed_widenings.justification: After a ranged attack with the weapon, it flies back to the thrower's hand immediately. No existing atom models weapon auto-return. This is a post-attack lifecycle effect with no current analog.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Immediately after you make a ranged attack with the weapon, it flies back to your hand.

proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_reaction_trigger
proposed_widenings.justification: Attack Deflection is a reaction triggered by 'being hit by an attack' — structurally identical to the Shield spell's trigger. TriggeredReactionMechanics exists only as a spell family. MagicItemMechanics is restricted to PassiveMechanics | ActivatedAbilityMechanics. ActivatedAbilityMechanics has activationCost: reaction but no trigger predicate (no 'when hit by attack' condition). A triggered-reaction subgraph for magic items is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you are hit by an attack while holding the weapon, you can take a Reaction to twirl the weapon around you, gaining a +5 bonus to your Armor Class against the triggering attack.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_ac_vs_triggering_attack
proposed_widenings.justification: The +5 AC from Attack Deflection applies specifically against the triggering attack — it is a retroactive modification to whether that single attack hit. This is distinct from modify_ac (which modifies AC generally for the spell/effect's duration). The Shield spell encodes this as modify_ac on a triggered_reaction, but the per-attack scoping needs explicit surfacing to be honest.
proposed_widenings.evidence: gaining a +5 bonus to your Armor Class against the triggering attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

notes: The dominant blocker is the form-conditional property system — three item forms with form-gated grant sets. No existing family can represent this. Even if form-switching were solved, the +2 damage bonus (missing damage_roll RollKind), the Thrown property grant, the auto-return atom, and the magic-item reaction trigger are additional independent gaps. The Acrobatic Assist (+Advantage on Acrobatics) could encode cleanly via modify_roll_advantage with skillFilter, but it is form-conditional and therefore blocked by the form-state machine gap. Light emission is narrative/environmental and is appropriately omitted even in a future encoding.
